newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE wheat firms in active trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE wheat firms in active trade.

text.p: LIFFE wheat futures firmed in active trade.
On the new crop buyers were speculating on weather worries, both local and worldwide, traders said.
The sellers were mainly shippers who were buying cheaper physical contracts and selling London futures, one trader said.
They made November the most active month on wheat, with 427 of a total 1,200 lots. It last traded 0.25 stg higher at 99.85 stg.
On the old crop market players had been able to roll positions on May forward. "It takes the pressure off the May," the trader said, allowing it to rise.

New estimates for old crop export availability, announced by the Home Grown Cereals Authority, were too late to have much effect on Wednesday. "The market was only just starting to take notice at the death," the trader said. He definitely thought the numbers would be a bearish element on Thursday.
The figures show export avvailability at 4.36 million tonnes, up from the previous estimate of 4.2 million.
On barley, November dominated, with 52 of the total 53 lots. It last traded 0.60 stg higher at 96.85 stg. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
